items.heading: Veterinary Medicine Is Not Shrinking,
items.text: Veterinary medicine is not shrinking, and it is not a soft, animal-themed side door into human medicine. It sits at the centre of India's dairy and poultry economy, the world's largest by milk volume, and it now also sits at the centre of a genuinely booming urban pet-care market. Neither of those facts is going away.

items.heading: Ask Five People Whether Veterinary
items.text: Ask five people whether veterinary is a good career and the answers will split hard, and the split is not random.

items.heading: Strip Away the Title
items.text: Strip away the title and the job is this: you handle animals that cannot describe their symptoms, make judgment calls with incomplete information, and explain those calls to a farmer or pet owner who is often anxious, grieving, or financially stretched.

rows: Roughly 5,300 seats across 53 VCI-approved government colleges in 24 states and union territories
Most seats sit inside state-domicile quota, so the real competition for an out-of-state candidate is the smaller All India Quota, not the full seat count.
All India Quota (open to any state)
Roughly 734 seats nationally (about 15% of government seats)
A NEET score near 520+ is generally the competitive band for a General-category AIQ seat; state-quota cutoffs run lower and vary sharply by state.
Rs 85,000-1.5 lakh a year on a state-quota seat; Rs 2.5-5 lakh a year on a management-quota seat
A management-quota seat over 5.5 years can cost Rs 12-25 lakh total before living costs, a number worth weighing hard against the entry pay bands above.
5.5 years, including one compulsory internship year
The internship year usually pays little to nothing, so the realistic runway to a first real paycheque is closer to six years after Class 12, not five.

items.heading: One Camp Pictures a Metro
items.text: One camp pictures a metro pet clinic, grateful pet owners, and a comfortable, respected practice. That picture is real for vets who build toward it deliberately, usually in a handful of cities.

items.heading: Another Camp Pictures Rural Dispensary
items.text: Another camp pictures rural dispensary rounds, vaccination drives, and modest government pay. That picture is also real, and it describes a large share of India's actual veterinary workforce and infrastructure.

items.heading: A Third Camp Treats
items.text: A third camp treats the whole field as a consolation prize for missing an MBBS rank. That framing does real damage, because it puts students with no genuine interest in animal health into a demanding, hands-on profession they never actually wanted.
